statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00Z on Friday and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is 42, moderate, because a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods reported at roughly $20 billion to $28 billion is now in force against a pledged dollar-for-dollar match, the latest H.15 curve prints 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year with the long bond at its highest since 2007, crude has completed a second consecutive weekly gain of about 5%, and a week carrying July PCE, Nvidia results and the Jackson Hole symposium waits on the other side of the halt; Confidence is 87 because the closing session, curve, volatility, energy and calendar evidence is verified and precise, with one index quote page disagreeing with two corroborating sources, and the only structurally missing input is a live price path that cannot exist while the venue is shut.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, reclaimed the entire decline to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, below its own open, with VIX at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range as the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. Both extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so none of the observed amplifiers that normally lift Tail above the block threshold are present. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly eight hours beyond the final slot published here, so every forward hour describes a closed market rather than a forecast price path. Weekend headline accumulation is real and is carried in Stress: tariffs in force with a matched Canadian response promised but unspecified, a 30-year yield at its highest since 2007 alongside pricing that carries a meaningful probability of a September hike, a standing energy premium, and a dense event week. Tail reflects the absence of a tradable path, not the absence of risk, and the first evidence about how these headlines are absorbed will arrive only after this horizon expires.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours while a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods meets a pledged dollar-for-dollar match, a 30-year yield at its highest since 2007 sits unpriced, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T15:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T14:00:00Z and end about eight hours before the reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, which is the observed profile of a functioning two-sided market rather than a pathological one-way path. One index quote page rendered a different set of session values during this run; two independent sources agreed on the figures published here, and the disagreement is reflected in a one-point reduction of Confidence to 87 rather than in the levels themselves. The wider week was harder: the Nasdaq lost about 2% and the S&P 500 about 1.4%, leaving the broad index roughly 2% below its record high, and the move was driven by Treasury volatility rather than by equity news. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release carries the latest curve at 4.19% on the 2-year, 4.39% on the 5-year, 4.69% on the 10-year and 5.23% on the 30-year, with the long bond at its highest yield since 2007 and market pricing reported at roughly a 35% probability of a September hike rising to about 66% by December. The rates move reached the index mainly through semiconductors, where the Philadelphia chips gauge fell about 5% on the week. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range on August expiry day. Cross-asset evidence from that session was conflicted rather than aligned: equities firmer, volatility lower, gold sharply higher and the long end weaker at the same time. Conflict of that kind weighs on Stress and on directional conviction, not on Tail. Weekend items have accumulated with no venue able to absorb them. The 50% US tariff took effect after midnight ET on Canadian goods reported at roughly $20 billion by one account and about $28 billion by others, Ottawa suspended negotiations and pledged a dollar-for-dollar match whose scope is not yet published. Energy remains the most persistent input, with WTI near $87.06 and Brent near $94.39 completing a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 5% while Strait of Hormuz transit stays disrupted. At the single-name level Tesla confirmed a recall of about three million vehicles in China over concealed door releases, an index-member headline of modest weight against a rates-driven tape. One offset is already announced rather than hypothetical: the Treasury will roughly double its liquidity-support buybacks in the 10- to 30-year sector from 9 September, well beyond this horizon. The week ahead is dense: July PCE, the second estimate of Q2 GDP and July durable goods all print together at 12:30Z on Wednesday, Nvidia reports after the US close the same day, coupon auctions fall on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and the Jackson Hole symposium runs 27-29 August with the Fed Chair keynote scheduled for Friday at 14:00Z alongside the preliminary annual payrolls benchmark revision. All of that is scheduled position rather than observed outcome, so it is recorded in the event calendar and carried in Stress. Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4 in every slot because a price path cannot be pathological when no price path can form, and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window, since a narrow evidence-based window cannot be drawn around a market that is not open. Shared Finviz cross-asset context collected at 15:02Z was fresh and complete and is used only as delayed latest-session confirmation of that mixed internal picture, never as live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-14 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout, so no hour approached the block threshold. The path tracks the session that produced it: 14 at 15:00Z on 21 August with an event/whipsaw reading during the afternoon repricing, 13 through the middle of the US session, a lift to 16 into the expiry close, then 10 at 20:00Z and 5 at 21:00Z as the venue shut. Every hour since has sat at the closed-venue floor of 4 with a normal dominant mode. Stress traced the mirror image, easing from 56 at the start of the window to 35 in the small hours of 22 August before firming back to 42 by 14:00Z as tariff, rates and energy headlines accumulated with no market able to price them. Confidence stayed in the 84-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T14:00:00Z and ends roughly eight hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds the closed-venue floor of 4 in every hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout, which reflects the absence of a tradable path rather than an absence of risk. Stress does the work instead. It starts at 42, eases to 40 through the thinning Saturday evening and the European overnight, then firms steadily to 44 in the final slots as the horizon closes on the reopen and on a week carrying July PCE, the second estimate of Q2 GDP and July durable goods together at 12:30Z on Wednesday, Nvidia results after the US close the same day, coupon supply on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and the Jackson Hole symposium from 27 to 29 August with the Fed Chair keynote on Friday at 14:00Z. That firming is calendar arithmetic and unpriced headline accumulation, not observed alignment. Confidence decays gently from 87 to 81 as the last live observation ages past a day and a half, which is ordinary staleness for a closed weekend rather than conflict between sources. Every forward slot is framed conditionally by construction, and the first genuine test of how the tariff, rates and energy stack is absorbed belongs to the sessions that can observe it.
